_comment: The one vocabulary. The parser, the renderer, the importer, the checks, README.md and the tests all read this file; tests/test_vocab.py fails when the code, the render or the README disagree with it, in either direction. Order is render order.

bug.doc: a bug of this repo's own, including one you caused and worked around
bug.heading: Own bugs

decision.doc: an open decision, with what it hinges on
decision.heading: Open decisions

suspicion.doc: an unconfirmed suspicion, with the probe that would settle it
suspicion.heading: Unconfirmed suspicions

report.doc: a problem reported to another repo's owner; its counterpart lives in their store
report.heading: Reported to other owners

temp.doc: an interim rule, with the check that retires it
temp.heading: Interim rules

note.doc: anything else worth keeping; the import default
note.heading: Notes

waiting-jacob.doc: needs Jacob's answer before anyone can move it

blocked.doc: waits on something other than Jacob; the evidence says what

done.doc: closed; the item lives in the history file from then on

code.doc: a change to the tool's own code

audit.doc: an audit or a check over the repo

tooling.doc: helpers, dev.sh subcommands, scripts around the tool

decision.doc: nothing to build until someone decides

research.doc: finding something out (reading, searching, comparing) before anything is built, filed or sent

labour.doc: work done by hand outside any code: driving, filing, sorting, a scan run once

outreach.doc: contacting a person or an organisation: a proposal, an appeal, a message (sending needs Jacob's yes first)

sizes._comment: An item's estimate (PLAN-small-tasks.md §2): a dispatch is one checkpoint, one done_when, one commit, one report. `ready: false` marks the one size too big for that: `todo ready` never lists it, `todo split` breaks it into children, and check fails it open with none. tools/usage reads this field for its `usage gate` estimate (§4.4).

S.doc: one step: one change, its test, one commit

M.doc: a few steps, still one checkpoint: one done_when, one commit, one report

L.doc: more than one checkpoint: `todo split` it into S and M children before anyone starts it

brief._comment: What every `todo brief` carries besides the item (PLAN-small-tasks.md §2.3, §3.5, §4.1): `stop_rule` is the plan's words, verbatim (tests/test_handoff.py holds them equal when the plan is present). `iterate_rule` is §3.5 worded to the shared runner's real commands (tools/checks checkslib/parts.py), not the plan's sketch: each backticked command in it must be `./dev.sh check` plus options the runner's `run` takes, or `./dev.sh test <part>` (dev.sh's `check --only <part>`), held to the runner's `usage --json` (tests/test_handoff.py IterateRule).
brief.stop_rule: Commit after each step that passes. If the full check fails twice, stop and report what passed, what failed and where. Do not start the suite a third time.
brief.iterate_rule: Iterate small, then run whole once. While fixing one thing, run only what it touches: where dev.sh hands its parts to the shared runner (parts.py), `./dev.sh test <part>` runs that one part, and `./dev.sh check --resume` re-runs only the parts whose files changed since they passed or that did not pass; where it does not, run the one test you changed by itself. Run the full suite once, before the commit: `./dev.sh check`, without --resume. The plan's check --quick does not exist: --resume is the runner's nearest.

approval._comment: Who may approve work for dispatch (the `approved` field's `by`): Jacob alone. `todo approve` writes this value and nothing else; check fails an `approved` whose `by` differs.

rule._comment: Approval by rule (PLAN-todo-tool.md §10.1 cause 1, TD-B1, approved by Jacob 2026-10-12): an open item (roles.default_status) counts as approved, with no `todo approve`, when its kind is one of `kinds`, its repo is its store's own, its size is one of `sizes`, every field in `needs` is set, its work is not one of `exclude_works`, and none of its `files` matches a glob in `exclude_files` (fnmatch: `*` crosses `/`). Read by todolib/approval.py alone. Judged afresh at every read; stored only by `todo dispatch` while the item is dispatched, as {by, date: `approved`, source: `source`}, so the source tells it from Jacob's own yes. The rule sees settings, a new remote or an outward act only through work and files.

waits_on._comment: What a waiting-jacob item (roles.jacob_status) waits on (PLAN-todo-tool.md §10.2 step 2): the field is `<value>`, or `<value>:<argument>` for a value whose `argument` is a regex the argument must match (null: it takes none). `clears` is the one pointer `todo blockers` prints for the group ({arg} is the argument). `todo add`, `edit` and `import` refuse a waiting-jacob item without one; check lists an older one that lacks it, and fails none.

wizard.doc: his answer to a question in a wizard definition, the argument

settings.doc: a settings step only he takes, such as applying a proposed settings file; the item's evidence says which
settings.clears: his settings step (each item's evidence names it)

approval.doc: his yes to start the work

decision.doc: his answer to a decision written in a plan section, the argument (FILE §n)

blockers._comment: `todo blockers` (PLAN-todo-tool.md §10.2 step 1, §10.4): every open item that is not dispatchable, grouped by its root. `roots` are the kinds of root, in tie-break order (roots rank by how many items wait behind them, then by this order); tests/test_blockers.py holds them equal to the kinds the code finds, both ways. The bounds are the text output's: the top `max_roots` roots, `max_ids` ids per root, and `dispatchable_lines` lines of it under `todo dispatchable` when nothing is dispatchable. --json is unbounded.

jacob.doc: his answer, approval or settings step: a waiting-jacob item's waits_on (an item naming none is grouped as such), or an item ready but for his approval

item.doc: the open item at the end of a blocked_by chain, followed to its end; an id no scanned store holds, or a cycle, is a root of its own

owner.doc: a report: another store's counterpart, by its id there (or the report not yet written)

field.doc: what `todo brief` needs and the item lacks (repo, work, done_when, a size it can be dispatched at), or a blocked status naming no blocked_by: the store's owner triages it

resolutions._comment: Resolution values with a meaning of their own; any other resolution is free text written by `todo done`. Each is named by a role, set only where that role says, and refused everywhere else.

done-deprecated.doc: an imported closed bullet (DONE marker, or a Resolved or Confirmed heading) that carried no resolution; set by `todo import` only, refused by `todo done`, and red in check on an item not imported (Jacob, td-1, 2026-10-04)

fields._comment: Every item carries every field, unset ones null; an `optional` field was added after items existed, so an item written before it may lack the key (read as null). History is append-only, so its old entries never gain the key; new items always carry it.

id.doc: repo prefix + counter, stable, never reused (todo:td-3 points at it)

evidence.doc: what you ran, what you saw, what you concluded; may span lines

probe.doc: the run that would settle a suspicion
probe.label: probe

reported_to.doc: {repo, date, their_id}: whom it was reported to, and the counterpart's id there
reported_to.label: reported to

parent.doc: any item's id, in any scanned repo, open or closed
parent.label: parent

blocked_by.doc: ids of the items that must close first, in any scanned repo; `todo ready` leaves the item out until every one is in history
blocked_by.label: blocked by

waits_on.doc: what a waiting-jacob item waits on: `<value>` or `<value>:<argument>`, a value of `waits_on` below; set by `todo add/edit --waits-on` or by `todo import`, and required on a waiting-jacob item (an older one is listed by check); `todo blockers` groups by it, never by prose
waits_on.label: waits on

repo.doc: where the work lives: a repo name, never an agent
repo.label: repo

size.doc: one of the sizes, the estimate `todo ready` and tools/usage read; null until someone sizes it, and an unsized item is never ready
size.label: size

handoff.doc: {date, text, commit}: the last checkpoint's note (done; next; how to verify), the day it was written and the work repo's commit then (null when that repo is not found); set by `todo edit ID --handoff`, carried by `todo brief`
handoff.label: handoff

approved.doc: {by, date, source}: Jacob's go-ahead to start the work (`by` is `approval.by` below), the day he gave it and where (his words, or a pointer to them); set by `todo approve`, or by `todo import` from "approved: Jacob <date>" in an item's lead (import.approval), read by `todo dispatchable`
approved.label: approved

dispatched.doc: {date, text}: the day the item was handed to someone to do, and an optional one-line note (never an agent's name: items name repos); set by `todo dispatch` only, cleared by `todo dispatch --clear` when it comes back unfinished; `todo dispatchable` leaves it out while set
dispatched.label: dispatched

retire.doc: the check that retires an interim rule
retire.label: retire

tags.doc: the tags set by hand, `<namespace>:<value>`, in the namespaces `tags` below marks `stored` (plan:, origin:, trust:, ref:); repo:, kind:, status:, todo.work: and the ref: of parent, blocked_by and reported_to are derived from the fields and never stored
tags.label: tags

plan_pins.doc: [{plan, digest, date}]: for each plan:PLAN-<name>.md§<n> tag, the sha256 of that section's text (read by `setup plans show`) and the day it was read; set by `todo add/edit --pin-plan` only, read by `todo stale-plans`, which lists the item once its section changes or is gone
plan_pins.label: plan pins

done.doc: date closed, YYYY-MM-DD; null while open (or when an imported DONE bullet carried no date)
done.label: done

resolution.doc: how it closed; null while open; done-deprecated for an imported closed bullet
resolution.label: resolution

imported.doc: {sha, section, title_from, sep}: set by todo import (the block's sha, its headings, where the title came from), null otherwise

tags._comment: Ids and tags (PLAN-services.md §3, PLAN-todo-tool.md §9 step 4). An item's id outside this tool is `<service>:<id>` (todo:td-3); every command taking an id also takes that form. `shared` is a local copy of the seven namespaces of PLAN-services.md §3's table, meaning for meaning: the shared vocabulary lives in the architecture service (S3), which does not exist yet, so this table is read from there once it does (TODO.md). `from` derives a namespace from an item field (never stored); `values` closes a namespace; `rule` names the form check in todolib/tags.py. `own` are this service's, under its prefix.

plan.doc: which plan section it serves: PLAN-<name>.md, optionally §<section>

kind.doc: what sort of thing it is

trust.doc: whether its text may be read as instructions

status.doc: its state in its owner's vocabulary

ref.doc: another record it points at, by id: `<service>:<id>`

import._comment: Kind and status of an imported block come from its section headings, deepest heading first, first rule that matches (case-insensitive, from a word start: `confirmed` does not match 'Unconfirmed'). A block whose own text starts with the done marker goes to history whatever its heading. `confirmed` → done: a confirmed finding is settled work (PLAN-todo-tool.md §9 step 1, td-22, Jacob 2026-10-09).
import._rules: What a block's text already says, read into fields (PLAN-todo-tool.md §10.2 step 6). The lead is the text up to its first blank line or nested list line. A rule that reads nothing sets nothing: the item is listed in the import's output instead, never given a guess.
import._approval: In the lead: sets `approved` {by: approval.by, date, source: the quoted words, else the matched text} and moves a waiting-jacob item to roles.default_status. A date after the import day is not applied; the item is listed.
import._waits_on: For a block still waiting-jacob after the approval rule: the earliest match in its text of any rule gives its waits_on (`value`, a template of the match). One with `plan` resolves only when that PLAN section reads (the plans CLI, as --pin-plan). A block naming none, or naming a pointer no rule resolves (`waits_on_mention` shows it), is listed; a real import then needs --waits-on.
import._probe: For a kind requiring `probe`: the text after the first marker, up to the first '.' outside backticks that ends a sentence.
import._report: For a kind requiring `reported_to`: the lead's first word, when it is the whole owner and a repo the scan finds (a store's repo, or a git repo folder's name), not this store's own. Date: the first `(YYYY-MM-DD` on its first line, else the import day. their_id: null (todo check then says how to pair it).

skip._comment: Not items: `intro`, a paragraph above a section's first bullet in a section holding bullets, and any paragraph under the top heading alone (or none); `heading_only`, a block whose whole text matches it. Each is counted and printed by the import, never dropped unseen.

import._fallback: A kind whose required field no rule reads imports as roles.default_kind, recording the kind it would have had in imported.wanted, and is listed with the todo edit that completes it.
